newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MAYOR WANTS VICENZA TO STAY LOCALLY-OWNED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MAYOR WANTS VICENZA TO STAY LOCALLY-OWNED.

text.p: The mayor of Vicenza, whose serie A soccer club could end up with English owners, said on Thursday that he hoped the northern Italian city's businessmen would win control.
Marino Quaresimin told Reuters that selling the club would be a defeat for Vicenza, with one of the highest per-capita incomes in Italy and plenty of wealthy businessmen.
"I hope that the city can find the will to get involved in Vicenza," he said in a telephone interview.

The club, who have qualified for next season's European Cup Winners' Cup, has a profitable balance sheet but will be auctioned to the highest bidder on Friday as a result of bankruptcy affecting the owners.

Newspaper reports have said that London-based investment company Stellican, closely linked to U.S. investment group Apollo, has made the highest bid. A successful bid by Stellican would make Vicenza the first foreign-owned soccer club in Italy.
Two Italian bids have also been made.

Stellican managing director Stephen Julius told the London Financial Times on Wednesday that his group wanted to redevelop the ageing Romeo Menti stadium, invest in new players and develop sponsorship and merchandising.
But he added that he was worried that a foreign takeover would prove unpopular with local fans.
Quaresimin was quoted in Italian newspapers on Thursday as suggesting that English owners could not take for granted the use of the council-owned stadium.
The daily Corriere della Sera had quoted him under a headline: "No stadium, they're English.
The mayor, who last week issued a statement appealing to the officially-appointed receivers to evaluate potential purchasers carefully, told Reuters his words were distorted.
"The description of "no stadium" was a misrepresentation of my words," he said. "Vicenza soccer club is close to my heart."
"It's hard to say 'no, I won't give it to you'. Where else would they go? Trieste? Verona?...If the English win, I will have to take note."
In last week's statement, Quaresimin said the city's image was at stake as well as the fate of the club.
"The moment is extremely delicate. It's important and I would say necessary for the club to be handed over to owners with a significant number of 'Vicentini' (local people) involved."
